feedback.worked_solution:
The Wronskian $W({x}_{1},{x}_{2})$ of two vector-valued functions 

$$
{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{11}(t) \\ {x}_{21}(t)\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{12}(t) \\ {x}_{22}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

is defined as

$$
W({x}_{1},{x}_{2})=det({x}_{1},{x}_{2})=|\begin{aligned}{x}_{11}(t) & {x}_{12}(t) \\ {x}_{21}(t) & {x}_{22}(t)\end{aligned}|.
$$

Note the following:

- If the Wronskian is not identically zero, then ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are linearly independent.

- If the Wronskian is identically zero, and it's known that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are solutions to the same system of linear ODEs, then ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are linearly dependent.

In our case, our Wronskian is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}W({x}_{1},{x}_{2}) & =|\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -3\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 3\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}| \\  & =(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot (2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)-(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot (3\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =4{cos}^{2}⁡t+9{sin}^{2}⁡t \\  & =4{cos}^{2}⁡t+9{sin}^{2}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

which is $\text{nonzero for at least one }t\in R.$

Therefore, the set ${{x}_{1}(t),{x}_{2}(t)}$ is linearly $\text{independent}$ on $R.$

submitted_fields.submitted_value: nonzero for at least one $t\in R$
